name: SC16IS740IPW_Q900,
title: Single UART bridged to an I2C-bus or SPI slave port, 64-byte FIFOs, IrDA SIR
summary: SC16IS740, SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 put one full-duplex UART with 64-byte receive and transmit FIFOs behind a slave I2C-bus (400 kbit/s) or SPI (mode 0) port, chosen by a pin. The register set follows the 16C450 and adds automatic RTS/CTS and Xon/Xoff flow control, RS-485 direction control and address detection, an IrDA SIR encoder and decoder, and a sleep mode under 30 µA. The SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 add eight programmable I/O pins, four of which can serve as modem lines; the SC16IS760 also runs SPI to 15 Mbit/s and IrDA SIR to 1.152 Mbit/s. The SC16IS740 comes in TSSOP16, the other two in TSSOP24 and HVQFN24; SC16IS740IPW/Q900 is the AEC-Q100 version.

tables.title: FIFO Control Register (FCR) bits
rows: TX FIFO trigger level: 00 = 8, 01 = 16, 10 = 32, 11 = 56 spaces; an enhanced function, writable only with EFR[4] = 1
1 empties the transmit FIFO and resets its level logic (the transmit shift register is left alone); clears itself afterwards. 0 = no reset (default)
1 empties the receive FIFO and resets its level logic (the receive shift register is left alone); clears itself afterwards. 0 = no reset (default)
1 = transmit and receive FIFOs on; 0 = both off (default)
notes: Write-only register.
(1) A FIFO reset takes at least two XTAL1 clocks, so it needs the XTAL1 clock running.

tables.title: Line Control Register (LCR) bits
rows: break control: 1 holds TX at logic 0 to send a break until the bit is cleared; 0 = no break (default)
forced parity (with LCR[3] = 1): 0 = not forced (default); with LCR[4] = 0 parity is forced to 1, with LCR[4] = 1 it is forced to 0, on both transmit and receive
parity enable: 0 = none (default); 1 = parity bit sent and checked on receive
stop bits: 0 = 1 stop bit; 1 = 1.5 stop bits with 5-bit words, 2 stop bits with 6, 7 or 8-bit words

tables.title: Line Status Register (LSR) bits
rows: FIFO data error: 1 while any parity error, framing error or break is anywhere in the RX FIFO; clears when none remain. 0 = no error (default)
transmitter empty: 1 when both THR and TSR are empty
THR empty: 1 when the transmit holding register is empty; with the FIFO on, up to 64 characters may then be loaded
break interrupt: 1 when RX was LOW for one character frame, received as 0x00. 0 = none (default)
framing error: 1 when the character at the top of the RX FIFO had no valid stop bit. 0 = none (default)
parity error in the character at the top of the RX FIFO. 0 = none (default)
overrun error: 1 when an overrun occurred. 0 = none (default)
data in receiver: 1 when the RX FIFO holds at least one character. 0 = empty (default)
notes: LSR[4:2] belong to the character waiting at the top of the RX FIFO, so reading LSR first and RHR second pairs each error with its character; an empty RX FIFO gives 0 in all three.

tables.title: Modem Control Register (MCR) bits
rows: clock divisor: 0 = input clock ÷ 1, 1 = input clock ÷ 4
loopback: 1 = internal loopback, TX fed back to RX inside the chip and MCR[1:0] fed to MSR[4:5]; 0 = normal
1 makes TCR and TLR reachable; 0 hides them
RTS: 0 forces RTS inactive (HIGH), 1 forces it active (LOW). Drives MSR[4] in loopback. With auto RTS on, flow control drives the pin instead
DTR (2): with GPIO5 set as DTR through IOControl bit 1, 0 forces DTR inactive (HIGH) and 1 forces it active (LOW); IOState bit 5 then has no effect on the pin
notes: (1) MCR[7:5] and MCR[2] change only while EFR[4] = 1.
(2) SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only.

tables.title: Modem Status Register (MSR) bits
rows: CD (1), active HIGH: the inverse of the CD input when GPIO6 is set as CD through IOControl bit 1; IOState bit 6 does not show the pin then
RI (1), active HIGH: the inverse of the RI input when GPIO7 is set as RI through IOControl bit 1
DSR (1), active HIGH: the inverse of the DSR input when GPIO4 is set as DSR through IOControl bit 1; IOState bit 4 does not show the pin then
CTS, active HIGH: the inverse of the CTS input
CD (1) changed state; cleared by reading
RI (1) went from LOW to HIGH; cleared by reading
DSR (1) changed state; cleared by reading
CTS changed state; cleared by reading
notes: (1) SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only.
The RI, CD, CTS and DSR pins are active LOW.

tables.title: Interrupt Enable Register (IER) bits
rows: modem status interrupt (2): 1 = enabled, 0 = disabled (default); the pins become modem lines through IOControl bit 1
receive line status interrupt: 1 = enabled, 0 = disabled (default)
notes: (1) IER[7:4] change only while EFR[4] = 1. Setting IER[1] again does not raise a new interrupt while the THR is below its threshold.
(2) SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only.

tables.title: Interrupt Identification Register (IIR) bits
rows: interrupt status: 0 = an interrupt is pending, 1 = none pending
notes: Read-only.

tables.title: Interrupt source
rows: CTS, RTS change of state from active (LOW) to inactive (HIGH)
notes: (1) Modem interrupt status is read in MSR; GPIO interrupt status in IOState.
(2) SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only.

tables.title: Enhanced Features Register (EFR) bits
rows: auto CTS: 1 = on, transmission stops while CTS is HIGH; 0 = off (default)
auto RTS: 1 = on, RTS goes HIGH at the RX FIFO halt level TCR[3:0] and LOW at the resume level TCR[7:4]; 0 = off (default)
special character detect: 1 = received data compared with Xoff2; a match goes into the FIFO and sets IIR[4]; 0 = off (default)
enhanced functions: 1 unlocks IER[7:4], FCR[5:4] and MCR[7:5] for writing; 0 locks them
software flow control mode (software flow control options table)

tables.title: Transmission Control Register (TCR) bits
rows: RX FIFO level at which transmission resumes
RX FIFO level at which transmission halts
notes: Levels run 0 to 60 characters in steps of 4.
Writable only with EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1. TCR[3:0] must be greater than TCR[7:4]; nothing in hardware checks it. Set TCR before turning on auto RTS or software flow control.

tables.title: Trigger Level Register (TLR) bits
rows: RX FIFO interrupt trigger, characters available (4 to 60)
TX FIFO interrupt trigger, spaces available (4 to 60)
notes: Writable only with EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1. The value written is the trigger level divided by 4.
A field of 0 hands that FIFO's trigger to FCR; a non-zero field overrides FCR. With TLR setting the RX trigger, FCR[7:6] stays at 00.

tables.title: Transmitter FIFO Level (TXLVL) bits
rows: free spaces in the TX FIFO, 0 (0x00) to 64 (0x40)
notes: Read-only.

tables.title: Receiver FIFO Level (RXLVL) bits
rows: characters held in the RX FIFO, 0 (0x00) to 64 (0x40)
notes: Read-only.

tables.title: I/O pin Direction (IODir) bits
rows: direction of GPIO7 to GPIO0, one bit each: 0 = input, 1 = output
notes: SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only. Writing IODir clears a pending GPIO interrupt.

tables.title: I/O pin State (IOState) bits
rows: write: level for each pin set as output (0 = low, 1 = high); read: the state of every pin
notes: SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only.

tables.title: I/O Interrupt Enable (IOIntEna) bits
rows: per input pin: 1 = a change raises an interrupt, 0 = it does not
notes: SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only. With GPIO[7:4] set as modem lines, their interrupts come through IER[3] and IOIntEna bits 7 to 4 do nothing.

tables.title: I/O Control (IOControl) bits
rows: software reset: writing 1 resets the device; the bit returns to 0
0 = GPIO[7:4] are I/O pins; 1 = they are RI, CD, DTR, DSR

input latching. 0: not latched; any input change interrupts, reading the input register clears it, and the interrupt also clears if the pin returns before that read. 1: latched; the changed level is held in IOState, only a read of IOState clears the interrupt, and the held value stays even if the pin returns first
notes: SC16IS750 and SC16IS760 only (the SC16IS740 has the software reset bit alone).
As I/O pins, GPIO4 to GPIO7 follow IODir, IOState, IOIntEna and IOControl; CD, RI and DSR then do not appear in MSR and raise no modem interrupt, and MCR[0] does not drive DTR.

As modem lines, CD, RI and DSR read in MSR[7:5] and MSR[3:1], DTR follows MCR[0], a change on RI, CD or DSR raises a modem interrupt when IER[3] is set, and bits 7:4 of IODir, IOState and IOIntEna have no effect.

tables.title: Extra Features Control Register (EFCR) bits
rows: 0 = IrDA SIR, 3/16 pulse width, up to 115.2 kbit/s; 1 = IrDA SIR, 1/4 pulse width, up to 1.152 Mbit/s (1)
RS-485 RTS polarity: 0 = RTS 0 while transmitting and 1 while receiving; 1 = the reverse
1 = the transmitter drives RTS; 0 = it does not
1 = transmitter off: nothing leaves TX, the TX FIFO keeps filling from the host until full, and a character already in the TSR finishes first; 0 = on
1 = receiver off at once, the character in the shift register still going to the RX FIFO; 0 = on. Setting it mid-reception is not advised
notes: (1) SC16IS760 only.

circuits.title: 1.8432 MHz crystal oscillator
circuits.description: The on-chip oscillator runs a 1.8432 MHz crystal placed between XTAL1 and XTAL2. Each crystal end has a capacitor to ground: 22 pF on the XTAL1 side and 33 pF on the XTAL2 side.

where.prescaler: 1 with MCR[7] = 0 (the reset state), 4 with MCR[7] = 1

where.tw3: period of the clock on XTAL1 (tw1 + tw2)

operation.text: The three parts share one UART design. The SC16IS740 is an SC16IS750 without the eight I/O pins. The SC16IS760 is an SC16IS750 with SPI clock to 15 Mbit/s (against 4 Mbit/s) and IrDA SIR to 1.152 Mbit/s (against 115.2 kbit/s); otherwise the two match in function and electrical figures.

I2C/SPI HIGH selects the I2C-bus: SCL and SDA with A0 and A1 setting one of 16 addresses; SO is left open. I2C/SPI LOW selects SPI: SCLK, CS, SI and SO, with SDA tied to VSS. Both ports are slave only.
Slave only, up to 400 kbit/s (fast mode), with a noise filter on SCL and SDA. A bus time-out resets the serial interface if SDA stays LOW for 25 ms or more.

A write is: START, slave address with W, the register address byte, then one or more data bytes, then STOP. A read sends the slave address with W and the register address byte, then a repeated START and the slave address with R; data bytes follow, each ACKed by the host, the last one NACKed, then STOP. In the register address byte bits 6:3 pick the register and bits 2:1 are 00.

SPI mode 0, slave only. Each access starts with one byte: bit 7 R/W (1 = read), bits 6:3 the register address, bits 2:1 the channel (00), bit 0 unused, followed by the data byte. Keeping CS LOW and clocking more bytes after a THR (0x00) write or an RHR read streams data into the TX FIFO or out of the RX FIFO.

Receive and transmit FIFOs each hold 64 characters; the receive FIFO also keeps three error bits per character. Both FIFOs are off after reset, which leaves a trigger level of one character. The FIFO is still used for the transmitted byte when off; a full FIFO loses further characters. TXLVL and RXLVL report the fill state.
Interrupt trigger levels come from FCR (fixed choices) or from TLR (4 to 60 in steps of 4). When the TLR field is zero FCR applies; when it is non-zero TLR applies.

Auto CTS and auto RTS are switched separately by EFR[7:6]. With auto CTS the transmitter sends a character only while CTS is LOW; CTS rising before mid-way through the final stop bit lets the present character finish and holds back the next. With auto RTS, RTS goes HIGH when the RX FIFO reaches the halt level in TCR[3:0] and returns LOW at the resume level in TCR[7:4] (FCR levels are used when TCR is zero). The far end may still send one more character after RTS rises. With both on and RTS of each UART wired to CTS of the other, no overrun can happen. CTS changes raise no host interrupt while auto CTS is on.

EFR[3:0] choose which Xon/Xoff characters are sent and compared (one pair, the other, or both in sequence). An Xoff received stops transmission after the current character, sets IIR[4] if IER[5] allows and pulls IRQ LOW; the matching Xon clears it. Xoff goes out when the RX FIFO passes the halt level (TCR[3:0] or FCR[7:6]); Xon goes out at the resume level. With a 5, 6 or 7-bit word only that many low bits of the Xon/Xoff characters are sent. Xon Any (MCR[5]) resumes on any received character. Special character detect (EFR[5]) compares incoming data with Xoff2, sets the Xoff interrupt without halting, and stores the character in the RX FIFO; reading IIR clears it. Hardware and software flow control are not meant to run together.

Power-on reset, the RESET pin and the software reset bit do the same thing. DLL, DLH, SPR and the four Xon/Xoff registers keep their values. After reset TX and RTS are HIGH, the I/O pins are inputs and IRQ is released.

Wait at least 3 µs after power-up (internal power-on reset) before the first bus access; an external RESET pulse may also be applied. Registers can then be read and written, but the UART transmitter and receiver need a stable clock on XTAL1. A crystal can take a few milliseconds to start, depending on the crystal, the supply ramp and the load capacitors.

Seven priority levels, enabled through IER and IOIntEna and reported in IIR[5:0]. Receive line status interrupts come from LSR[7], set while any error is in the RX FIFO. The receive time-out fires four character times after the last character when the FIFO holds data below the trigger level; the counter restarts at the centre of each received stop bit and on each FIFO read. An Xoff interrupt from flow control clears on the next Xon; one from special character detect clears on reading IIR. Interrupt mode uses IRQ when any of IER[3:0] is set; with IER[3:0] = 0000 the host polls LSR.

Enabled when EFR[4] and IER[4] are both 1. The UART sleeps, its clock stopped, once RX is idle, the TX FIFO and shift register are empty, the RX FIFO is empty and no interrupt other than THR is pending. It wakes on activity on RX, a change on a modem input, or a write to the TX FIFO. Revision C and D devices do not wake from RX data in IrDA mode (application note AN10964 gives a workaround); revision E does. GPIO transitions do not wake it, but GPIO inputs can still be read and GPIO interrupts still work. Clear IER[4] before writing DLL or DLH.
A break is detected when RX stays LOW longer than one full character with its start, parity and stop bits. Setting LCR[6] sends a break by holding TX LOW until the bit is cleared.

XTAL1 divided by 1 or 4 (MCR[7]) and then by the 16-bit DLH:DLL divisor gives the 16× clock for both transmit and receive. Choose the crystal tolerance to keep the baud rate error under 1 %; a 100 ppm crystal is generally recommended.
XTAL1 takes a crystal (up to 24 MHz) with XTAL2, or an external clock up to 80 MHz at 3.3 V or 48 MHz at 2.5 V, with XTAL2 open.

The four address bits reach the general set while LCR[7] = 0. With LCR[7] = 1 (and LCR not 0xBF), addresses 0x00 and 0x01 give DLL and DLH. With LCR = 0xBF, the enhanced set (EFR, XON1, XON2, XOFF1, XOFF2) appears. TCR and TLR take the place of MSR and SPR when EFR[4] = 1 and MCR[2] = 1.

Setting EFCR[4] gives the transmitter control of RTS, above MCR[1] and hardware flow control: RTS goes to 0 when the host writes to the TX FIFO and back to 1 after the last bit has gone out. EFCR[5] inverts this. Hardware flow control is turned off to use it.

EFCR[0] enables 9-bit mode, with flow control off. Address characters carry parity 1. In normal multidrop mode (EFR[5] = 0) the receiver is set to forced parity 0 (LCR[5:3] = 111): an address character shows as a parity error, raises a line status interrupt (IER[2] = 1) and enters the RX FIFO, and the host turns the receiver on or off depending on whether the address is its own. With auto address detection (EFR[5] = 1, address in XOFF2) the receiver drops everything until an address matching XOFF2 arrives, then turns itself on and stores it with its parity bit in the error bit position; a non-matching address later turns the receiver off again.

The built-in IrDA SIR encoder and decoder is selected by MCR[6]. The SC16IS750 runs 3/16 pulses up to 115.2 kbit/s; the SC16IS760 adds 1/4 pulses up to 1.152 Mbit/s (EFCR[7]). SIR at 1.152 Mbit/s does not interoperate with IrDA MIR at that speed.

SC16IS750 and SC16IS760: GPIO0 to GPIO7 are set as inputs or outputs in IODir, driven and read through IOState, and can interrupt on input change (IOIntEna), with optional latching (IOControl bit 0). Each input has an active pull-up of 3.02 MΩ to 4.91 MΩ. IOControl bit 1 turns GPIO4 to GPIO7 into DSR, DTR, CD and RI.
5, 6, 7 or 8 data bits; even, odd, forced or no parity; 1, 1.5 or 2 stop bits. Transmitter and receiver can each be disabled (EFCR[2:1]); internal loopback is in MCR[4].
IRQ is open-drain and needs an external pull-up to VDD: 1 kΩ for 3.3 V, 1.5 kΩ for 2.5 V.

On HVQFN24 the die ground connects to both VSS pins and the exposed pad. The VSS pins must go to ground; the pad is soldered to a matching board pad with thermal vias for heat and electrical performance.
All pins carry ESD protection for normal handling; JESD625-A precautions apply.
